## Findings: unvalidated input in Gitea's API handlers

This is a static read of the code. I did not build or run anything, and I did not reproduce any of these. Paths are relative to the repo root. Binding tags (`binding:"..."`) are the main validation mechanism, so I checked each finding against them and against the service layer.

**Coverage:** I covered `routers/api/v1` (repo files, branches/refs, commits, wiki, teams, milestones, labels, releases, attachments, mirrors, and user/admin settings) and spot-checked `routers/api/packages`. I did not audit `routers/api/actions` or every v1 handler, so this is not exhaustive.

### 1. Git operations: missing sanitization

- **Commit trailers can be forged via identity fields.** `services/repository/files/temp_repo.go:316` (sign-off) and `:303` (co-author) write `committerSig.String()` raw into the commit message. That string is `Name <email>`, built from the API's `committer`/`author` fields. `modules/git/signature_nogogit.go:23-25` does no escaping, and `modules/structs/repo_commit.go:14-17` only length-bounds the fields (100 and 254). A name containing `\n` would add arbitrary trailer lines. I have not reproduced this, but the code path is clear.
- **Commit identity has no character validation at all.** The same `repo_commit.go:14-17` fields are passed to `services/repository/files/temp_repo.go:237-251`. The env-var path (`:320-321`) is safe because git strips `<`, `>`, and newlines from idents. The problem is the message body write above.
- **`CleanGitTreePath` only rejects `.git` components.** `services/repository/files/file.go:143-155` does not reject NUL or control characters. I did not verify whether git's index rejects them later.
- **SHA inputs skip the ref-pattern check in some handlers.** `routers/api/v1/repo/commits.go:359-360` (raw diff) and `routers/api/v1/repo/tree.go:59-64` pass the path `sha` straight to git without `git.IsValidRefPattern`, unlike `commits.go:66-67` and `notes.go:54-56`. Both resolve through `ConvertToGitID` (`modules/git/repo_commit_nogogit.go:114`), which runs `rev-parse --verify`, so I did not find an exploit. It is still an inconsistency.

### 2. Enum values not validated

- **Milestone state is silently coerced.** `routers/api/v1/repo/milestone.go:164` (create) and `:226` (edit) treat any value other than `"closed"` as open. `modules/structs/issue_milestone.go:45` and `:56` are plain strings with no `In(...)` binding.
- **File operation enum is enforced late.** `modules/structs/repo_file.go:76` binds only `Required`, though the comment lists the enum. The real check is `services/repository/files/update.go:248-249`, which returns a plain `fmt.Errorf`. `routers/api/v1/repo/file.go:596` turns that into a 500 instead of a 422.
- **Object format is enforced late, with the same 500 problem.** `modules/structs/repo.go:168` has only `MaxSize(6)`. The real check is `services/repository/create.go:227-228` (plain error), which reaches `routers/api/v1/repo/repo.go:264` as a 500.
- **Team unit keys and permissions are not validated.** `routers/api/v1/org/team.go:172-173` calls `unit_model.TypeFromKey` and `perm.ParseAccessMode` directly. An unknown key is stored as `TypeInvalid` (`models/unit/unit.go:364`). An unknown permission silently becomes `AccessModeNone` (`models/perm/access_mode.go:46-57`). `FindUnitTypes` (`models/unit/unit.go:346-356`) already exists to catch this and is not used here.

### 3. Integer bounds

- **Unbounded `limit` in wiki pages.** `routers/api/v1/repo/wiki.go:290` has only a lower bound. The loop at roughly `:296-310` calls `GetCommitByPath` once per entry in range, so the cost scales with `limit` up to the page count. `maxNum := page * limit` can also overflow.
- **Unbounded `limit` in issue dependencies.** `routers/api/v1/repo/issue_dependency.go:316-317` has the same issue.

Checked and fine: `services/repository/files/tree.go:47-50` clamps `per_page`. `models/db/list.go:63-73` and `:88-99` clamp page size and absolute list options. `services/convert/utils.go:15-22` clamps paged results (cargo and composer). npm's `from`/`size` go through `NewAbsoluteListOptions`.

### 4. String length

No `MaxSize` binding on these fields. Most of them rely on DB column limits, which I did not verify:

- **File content and messages:** `modules/structs/repo_file.go:12` (`Message`), `:43`, `:63`, `:81` (`ContentBase64`), `:102` (`ApplyDiffPatchFileOptions.Content`), `:83` and `:85` (`ChangeFileOperation.SHA` and `FromPath`, which lacks the `MaxSize(500)` that `:65` has).
- **Issues:** `modules/structs/issue.go:92` (`Title`, `Required` only) and `:111`. Handler: `routers/api/v1/repo/issue.go:579` and `:731-732`.
- **Labels:** `modules/structs/issue_label.go:30` (`Required` only) and `:45`. Handler: `routers/api/v1/repo/label.go:157` and `:217-218`.
- **Milestones:** `modules/structs/issue_milestone.go:37` and `:51`. Handler: `routers/api/v1/repo/milestone.go:159` and `:216-217`.
- **Releases:** `modules/structs/release.go:51`, `:55`, `:57`, `:71`, `:73`. Handler: `routers/api/v1/repo/release.go:267`, `:294`, `:366-367`.
- **Attachments:** `modules/structs/attachment.go:34` (`EditAttachmentOptions.Name`). Handlers: `routers/api/v1/repo/issue_attachment.go:183-186` (the `?name=` query overrides the filename) and `:269-270`, and `routers/api/v1/repo/release_attachment.go:229-231` and `:337-338`.
- **Git hook content:** `modules/structs/git_hook.go:22`, written at `routers/api/v1/repo/git_hook.go:141`. This is a script by design, so the risk is only the lack of a size bound.

### Checked and not findings

- Hook names are allowlisted (`modules/git/hook.go:45`).
- Webhook type is validated (`routers/api/v1/utils/hook.go:83`).
- Reactions are validated against the allowlist (`models/issues/reaction.go:223`).
- Archive type is switched with a default error (`routers/api/v1/repo/download.go:42-51`).
- Ref filters get a `refs/` prefix (`routers/api/v1/utils/git.go:84-86`).
- Wiki paths are sanitized (`services/wiki/wiki_path.go:144-149`, `QueryEscape` encodes the slashes).
- Fork names are validated downstream (`services/repository/create.go:338`).
- Issue and PR state are validated (`routers/api/v1/repo/issue.go:840`, `closeOrReopenIssue` at `:977`).
- Project template and card types are validated and return 422 (`services/convert/project.go`, `routers/api/v1/shared/project.go:483-493`).
- Mirror interval is validated (`routers/api/v1/repo/mirror.go:347-353`).
- Blob SHAs are parsed as hex (`modules/git/repo_blob.go:7-19`).

### Suggested priority

1. The commit-message trailer injection at `temp_repo.go:316` and `:303`. Strip newlines and `<`/`>` from identity names, and test it.
2. Team unit parsing at `org/team.go:172-173`. Reject invalid keys and permissions, using `FindUnitTypes` as the base.
3. Milestone state at `milestone.go:164` and `:226`. Validate against `open`/`closed` and return 422.
4. Return 422, not 500, for the operation and object-format errors (`update.go:248-249`, `create.go:227-228`).
5. Cap `limit` at `wiki.go:290` and `issue_dependency.go:317`.

## Findings: unvalidated input in Gitea API handlers

**Scope:** `routers/api/` contains `v1/` plus the non-versioned `packages/`, `actions/`, and `activitypub/` trees, so I covered those. I didn't read every handler. I used tag-level searches and read the high-risk paths in full, so treat this as a strong starting list, not a complete audit. Nothing was changed or executed.

**Mitigations confirmed (not findings):** branch and ref names use `GitRefName` (`modules/validation/binding.go:53`); secret and variable names go through `ValidateName` (`services/secrets/validation.go:25`); label colors use `NormalizeColor`; user and org renames use `IsUsableUsername` (`services/user/user.go:46`); `CleanGitTreePath` rejects `.git` components (`services/repository/files/file.go:143`); tag operations use `AddDashesAndList`, so user strings can't become git options; and `isSafeArgumentValue` blocks leading `-` (`modules/git/gitcmd/command.go:124`).

### Highest priority

1. **Newline reaches the `cat-file --batch` protocol stream.** `UpdateBranchRepoOption.NewCommitID` is only `Required` (`modules/structs/repo.go:324`). It flows through `services/repository/branch.go:510` into `ConvertToGitID`, then into `QueryInfo` on the non-gogit path (`modules/git/repo_commit_nogogit.go:131`). `QueryInfo` writes the string verbatim. Its newline guard only panics in dev/test builds (`modules/git/catfile_batch_command.go:59-61`, `modules/git/catfile_batch_legacy.go:68-70`). `isSafeArgumentValue` only checks for a leading `-` (`modules/git/gitcmd/command.go:124-126`). Impact is probably limited to desyncing one repo's batch process, which needs a repo writer. **Not verified by running it.**

2. **Release and tag names are never checked as git refs.** `CreateTagOption.TagName` and `CreateReleaseOption.TagName` are only `Required` (`modules/structs/repo_tag.go:56`, `modules/structs/release.go:49`). `CreateTag` passes the name straight to `CreateNewTag` (`routers/api/v1/repo/tag.go:197-210`). `CreateRelease` and `EditRelease` do the same (`routers/api/v1/repo/release.go:246-302`, `:360-361`). Neither service validates the name (`services/release/release.go:172-187`, `:223-245`). By contrast, the migration path enforces `git.IsValidRefPattern` and marks it as a security requirement (`services/migrations/gitea_uploader.go:271`, `modules/migration/release.go:31`). Git will reject most bad names, but the DB row and `LowerTagName` are written first, and there is no length bound.

3. **Unbounded commit IDs.** `NewCommitID` has no `MaxSize`, and `OldCommitID` has no binding at all (`modules/structs/repo.go:324`, `:327`). Both are passed to `rev-parse`, so this is a length issue rather than injection.

### Integer bounds

4. **Negative tracked time is accepted.** `AddTimeOption.Time` is `int64` with only `Required` (`modules/structs/issue_tracked_time.go:14`). The handler passes it through without a sign check (`routers/api/v1/repo/issue_tracked_time.go:202-235`), and `addTime` stores it as-is (`models/issues/tracked_time.go:197-208`). A negative entry reduces the issue's total time.

5. **Pagination `page` has no upper bound.** `GetListOptions` only clamps the minimum (`routers/api/v1/utils/page.go:13-18`). `(opts.Page-1)*opts.PageSize` can overflow for huge values (`models/db/list.go:44-46`), which would produce a negative offset and most likely a 500.

6. **Parse errors are silently dropped.** `FormInt` discards the `strconv.Atoi` error and returns 0 (`services/context/base_form.go:50-53`). Non-numeric `limit` or `page` values fall back silently with no 422.

### Enum values

7. **Unknown sort values silently fall back.** `sort` goes raw into `GetLabelsByRepoID` / `GetLabelsByOrgID`, which switch on it with a default (`routers/api/v1/repo/label.go:52`, `routers/api/v1/org/label.go:47`, `models/issues/label.go:432-441`, `:507`). The shared `ResolveSortOrder` returns 422 for bad values (`routers/api/v1/utils/sort.go:19-35`), so this is inconsistent.

8. **Unknown hook `type` is treated as "system".** `routers/api/v1/admin/hooks.go:53-59` maps any unrecognized value to the default.

9. **Event and branch filters are unvalidated.** `event` is cast straight to `HookEventType` (`routers/api/v1/shared/action.go:172-173`). `branch` goes through `RefNameFromBranch` with no ref check (`:176-177`). Both are probably parameterized, so impact is low.

10. **`operation` has no enum constraint at the struct level.** `ChangeFileOperation.Operation` is only `Required` (`modules/structs/repo_file.go:76`). The service does reject unknown values (`services/repository/files/update.go:229-249`, `:494-500`), so this is defense-in-depth only.

### String length (no `MaxSize`)

11. **Secret and variable values are unbounded.** `CreateOrUpdateSecretOption.Data` (`modules/structs/secret.go:25`) and `Value` (`modules/structs/variable.go:12`, `:28`) have no size limit. `CreateOrUpdateSecret` validates only the name (`services/secrets/secrets.go:13-16`), and `InsertEncryptedSecret` has no size check (`models/secret/secret.go:68-76`).

12. **Issue, comment, and PR text.** Issue title (`modules/structs/issue.go:92`), comment bodies (`modules/structs/issue_comment.go:40`, `:47`), and PR head, base, and title (`modules/structs/pull.go:124-128`) have no length bound. The storage limit depends on the DB column type; I didn't verify that.

13. **Other fields.** Label name (`modules/structs/issue_label.go:30`), project titles (`modules/structs/project.go:50`, `:89`), app names and redirect URIs (`modules/structs/user_app.go:37`, `:45`, `:51`), avatar `Image` (`modules/structs/user.go:113`), `BadgeSlugs` count (`modules/structs/user.go:136`), migration `CloneAddr` (`modules/structs/repo.go:394`), and workflow dispatch `Ref` (`modules/structs/repo_actions.go:53`, handler `routers/api/v1/repo/action.go:1174-1181`, which only checks for empty).

### File paths and packages

14. **`CleanGitTreePath` only checks the literal `.git` name.** It is case-insensitive, but it doesn't handle NTFS variants such as `.git.` or `.git ` (`services/repository/files/file.go:143-155`). Git's own path checks probably cover this. Applies to `update.go:131-146`. Defense-in-depth gap.

15. **Generic package version is only whitespace-checked.** `UploadPackage` checks the package name and filename, but the version only gets a trim check, with no length or charset rule (`routers/api/packages/generic/generic.go:86-90`). Download (`:37-41`) does no validation. Values are used as DB keys, not filesystem paths, so impact is low.

16. **Maven path segments aren't filtered.** `extractPathParameters` splits the wildcard path without rejecting `..` (`routers/api/packages/maven/maven.go:444-447`). The values are used as lookup keys, so I didn't count it as a finding.

### Recommended first fixes

- Add `GitRefName` and `MaxSize` to tag and release names, mirroring the migration checks (findings 2 and 3).
- Add a `^[0-9a-f]{40,64}$`-style check or `MaxSize(64)` to `NewCommitID` and `OldCommitID`, and reject `\n` in `ConvertToGitID` before `QueryInfo` (findings 1 and 3). Verify the exploit path before treating it as a vulnerability.
- Reject negative `AddTimeOption.Time` (finding 4) and cap `page` (finding 5).
- Return 422 for unknown `sort`, hook `type`, and `event` values, matching `ResolveSortOrder` (findings 7-9).

I audited the request structs and traced each suspicious input to its sink. Most candidates are already guarded downstream, so the real gaps are mostly bounds and enum checks at the binding layer. This is a read-only review: I changed nothing and committed nothing.

**Scope caveat:** `routers/api/v1` is the only versioned REST tree, and I reviewed it through its request structs (`modules/structs`) plus traced sinks, not by reading all 54k lines. `routers/api/actions` and `routers/api/packages` were only spot-checked.

## Findings

**1. Invalid file operation returns 500, not 422.** Medium.
- `modules/structs/repo_file.go:76`: `ChangeFileOperation.Operation` is `binding:"Required"` with no `In(...)` enum.
- `services/repository/files/update.go:249`: an unknown operation returns a plain `fmt.Errorf`.
- `routers/api/v1/repo/file.go:577-597`: `handleChangeRepoFilesError` doesn't match that error, so it falls through to `APIErrorInternal` (`:596`).
- Impact: a client error is reported as a server error. The enum belongs at the binding layer.

**2. Negative time-tracking durations accepted.** Medium.
- `modules/structs/issue_tracked_time.go:14`: `Time int64 binding:"Required"`. `Required` rejects 0 but not negative values.
- `routers/api/v1/repo/issue_tracked_time.go:202-235`: `form.Time` goes straight to `AddTime`.
- `models/issues/tracked_time.go:169`: `AddTime` has no sign check, so negative amounts are stored and written into a comment (`|%d`).

**3. Milestone `state` and `title` are unvalidated.** Medium.
- `modules/structs/issue_milestone.go:37` (`CreateMilestoneOption.Title`) and `:51` (`EditMilestoneOption.Title`): no `Required` or `MaxSize`.
- `issue_milestone.go:45` and `:56` carry `// enum: ["open","closed"]` in comments only, with no binding.
- `routers/api/v1/repo/milestone.go:164`: create treats anything other than `"closed"` as open. `:225-226`: edit does the same and reopens the milestone on any other value. An unrecognized state is silently accepted rather than rejected.
- `milestone.go:216-217` and `:159`: the title is stored with no length check.

**4. Label name has no length limit.** Low-medium.
- `modules/structs/issue_label.go:30`: `CreateLabelOption.Name` is `binding:"Required"` with no `MaxSize`. The DB column width is unverified.
- `routers/api/v1/repo/label.go:150` normalizes color through `NormalizeColor`, so color is fine.

**5. Unbounded free-text and path-like fields.** Low.
- `modules/structs/repo_file.go:12` (`Message`), `:43` and `:81` (`ContentBase64`), and `:85` (`ChangeFileOperation.FromPath`) have no `MaxSize`. Line 65 does have `MaxSize(500)` on a sibling `FromPath`, so the bound is inconsistent.
- `repo_file.go:83` (`SHA`) has no format check. It is only compared for equality (`services/repository/files/update.go:380-385`), so it isn't a sink.
- `modules/structs/repo_wiki.go:46`: wiki `Title` has no `MaxSize`, so the derived filename length is unbounded. Path traversal is blocked by `validateWebPath` (`services/wiki/wiki_path.go:44`), called from `services/wiki/wiki.go:90`.

**6. Git hook body is unbounded (by design).** Informational.
- `routers/api/v1/repo/git_hook.go:96-140`: `hook.Content = form.Content` has no size limit.
- The route is gated by `reqAdmin()` (`routers/api/v1/api.go:1337`), and writing hook scripts is the intended admin feature.

I found three places where sign-in middleware is missing or applied unevenly. I only read the route registrations and the middleware definitions. I didn't run anything or try the endpoints. In all three cases, a later permission check probably stops anonymous callers, so I'd rate these as inconsistency and defence-in-depth gaps rather than confirmed exploitable bypasses.

**1. API artifact DELETE has no `reqToken()` — `routers/api/v1/api.go:1438`**
- `m.Delete("", reqRepoWriter(unit.TypeActions), repo.DeleteArtifact)` has no `reqToken()`.
- The nearby run mutations at `routers/api/v1/api.go:1420-1426` (`DELETE`, `rerun`, `cancel`, `approve`, …) all use `reqToken(), reqRepoWriter(...)`.
- `reqRepoWriter` is the only guard on the artifact route. It checks permission, not sign-in, so an anonymous caller gets 403 rather than the 401 "token is required" that the sibling routes return.
- The group at `routers/api/v1/api.go:1436` also puts `GET` (unauthenticated read) and `DELETE` on one path, so this is the "some methods only" pattern you asked about.

**2. API `/file-contents` POST has no `reqToken()` — `routers/api/v1/api.go:1593`**
- `GetFileContentsPost` is registered on a `Combo` that has only `reqRepoReader(TypeCode)`, with no `reqToken()` (the `Combo` starts at `routers/api/v1/api.go:1591`).
- The in-code comment says "the POST method requires 'write' permission", but I saw no middleware enforcing write or sign-in on this route.
- It is a read-by-POST endpoint, so exposure is probably limited to what `GET` already allows.
- Compare `/contents` at `routers/api/v1/api.go:1585`, where the mutating routes have `reqToken()`.

**3. Web `POST /{username}/{reponame}/topics` has no `reqSignIn` — `routers/web/web.go:1524`**
- This route is in a group with only `context.RepoAssignment, reqRepoAdmin, context.RepoMustNotBeArchived()` (`routers/web/web.go:1525`).
- Every other mutating repo group in this file includes `reqSignIn`, for example `routers/web/web.go:1430` and `routers/web/web.go:1481`.
- `RequireRepoAdmin` (`services/context/permission.go:78`) does check `!ctx.IsSigned`, and returns 404 for unsigned users, so anonymous callers are rejected today.
- That protection only exists inside `reqRepoAdmin`. A change to that helper would silently open the route.

**Checked and fine**
- The web wiki `POST` routes at `routers/web/web.go:1594` and `routers/web/web.go:1597` add `reqSignIn` per method on a `Combo` whose `GET` is public. That is an intentional per-method pattern.
- The web compare `POST` at `routers/web/web.go:1302` also adds `reqSignIn` per method.
- The web actions group at `routers/web/web.go:1552` uses `optSignIn`, and its mutating routes carry `reqRepoActionsWriter`. I did not trace what `ViewPost` does for anonymous users. It appears to return run data like the `GET`, but I didn't confirm that.

I did this by reading the route registrations in `routers/web/web.go` and `routers/api/v1/api.go`, not by running the app or testing any requests. I did not check `routers/api/actions`, packages, or the other API sub-routers.

I found one authorization gap. I checked a few dozen other endpoints and they were guarded correctly.

## Finding

**Pull request deadline can be changed without write access**
- `routers/api/v1/repo/pull.go:692-705` is the deadline block in `EditPullRequest`. It runs for anyone who passes the earlier check at `pull.go:655`, which accepts the PR's poster as well as repo writers.
- A PR author with no write permission on the repo can therefore set or remove the deadline with `PATCH /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{index}`. It has no write check of its own.
- The other deadline paths all require write access:
  - assignees, milestone and labels in the same function check `CanWrite(unit.TypePullRequests)` (`pull.go:716`, `pull.go:731`, `pull.go:748`);
  - `EditIssue` guards the deadline with `canWrite` (`routers/api/v1/repo/issue.go:763`);
  - the dedicated deadline endpoint requires `CanWriteIssuesOrPulls` (`issue.go:962`);
  - the web handler does the same (`routers/web/repo/issue.go:390`).
- Impact is limited to changing the due date on your own PR. It is still privilege creep.

## Checked and found properly guarded

- **API issue and PR handlers:**
  - `routers/api/v1/repo/issue_subscription.go:130` restricts changing another user's subscription to that user or a site admin.
  - Comment edit and delete check the comment's poster or write access (`issue_comment.go:575`, `issue_comment.go:680`).
  - Attachment writes go through `canUserWriteIssueAttachment` and `attachmentBelongsToRepoOrIssue` (`issue_attachment.go:348-410`).
  - `dismissReview` requires repo admin.
  - Review-comment resolve checks `CanMarkConversation`, and `CancelScheduledAutoMerge` checks merge permission (`pull.go:1347`).
- **Runners, tokens and orgs:**
  - Runner lookups are scoped by owner ID (`routers/api/v1/shared/runners.go`).
  - Access-token routes require `reqSelfOrAdmin` plus basic auth, and deletion is scoped to `ContextUser.ID` (`routers/api/v1/user/app.go:214`).
  - Org write routes use `reqOrgOwnership`, and team repo add/remove goes through `canManageRepoCollaboratorTeam`. Publicize and conceal are limited to the member themselves, an org owner, or an admin (`routers/api/v1/org/member.go:216-228`).
- **Web handlers:**
  - Title, content, ref and time-estimate edits check poster or writer.
  - Time tracking checks `CanUseTimetracker`, and deleting a time entry requires the entry's owner or a site admin (`routers/web/repo/issue_timetrack.go:74`).
  - Dependencies check read permission on the other repo.
  - Content-history soft delete and attachment delete are scoped to the right repo and issue.
  - Attaching files by UUID to an issue or comment is validated by `validateAttachmentForIssue`.

I did not audit the admin API, packages, projects, webhooks or the private (internal) routes.

I found one authorization gap, in the project-board API. The other handlers I checked enforce permission and ownership correctly. I read the code only and ran nothing, so the finding is not confirmed by a request.

## Finding: project-board issue endpoints don't require write access to the issue

**Endpoints:**
- `POST` and `DELETE` on `.../projects/{id}/columns/{column_id}/issues/{issue_id}`
- `POST` on `.../projects/{id}/issues/{issue_id}/move`

These exist under `/repos/{owner}/{repo}`, `/orgs/{org}` and `/user`.

**What goes wrong:**
- **Route guard** (`routers/api/v1/api.go:1754`, `:1820`): the only check is project write access. For repos that is `reqRepoWriter(unit.TypeProjects)`. For orgs it is `reqProjectsUnitAccess(AccessModeWrite)`.
- **Handler check** (`routers/api/v1/shared/project.go:114-148`, `findIssue`): the issue lookup only requires that the user can read the issue (`CanReadIssuesOrPulls`). It never requires write access to the issue.
- **The mutation** (`shared/project.go:1838` add, `:1961` remove): this calls `project_service.AddIssueToColumn` or `RemoveIssueFromColumn`, which reach `issues_model.IssueAssignOrRemoveProject` (`models/issues/issue_project.go:70`). That function writes to the issue's project membership and creates a timeline comment attributed to the caller. It does no permission check itself.
- **Web UI comparison** (`routers/web/repo/web.go:1368`, `:1370`): the web endpoint for the same operation requires `reqRepoIssuesOrPullsWriter`, `reqRepoProjectsReader` and `UpdateIssueProject`. So someone with Projects-write but only issue-read access is blocked in the web UI and allowed through the API.

**Who can exploit it:**
- A user with Projects-write but only issue-read on a repo can add or remove that repo's issues from its project boards. Each change leaves a comment on the issue.
- On org boards, `reqProjectsUnitAccess` is satisfied by Projects-write on any one org repo (`api.go:822-823`). That user can then change project membership of issues in other org repos where they only have read access.

**Fix:** in `findIssue` (or in `findColumnIssue` and `MoveProjectIssue`), also require `perm.CanWriteIssuesOrPulls(issue.IsPull)` on the issue's repo. For the repo-scoped path, use `ctx.Repo.Permission`.

**Moving an issue between columns:** the web board's drag-and-drop (`routers/web/shared/project/project.go:151`) doesn't require issue-write, so I'd treat the move endpoint (`shared/project.go:2103`) as lower severity. Add and remove are the real gap.

## Minor issue, not an authorization bypass

`getIssueCommentSafe` (`routers/api/v1/repo/issue_comment_attachment.go:361-363`) returns `nil` without writing a response when the user lacks read access. Callers such as the one at `:61` then return, so the client gets an empty 200 instead of a 403 or 404. It leaks nothing and grants nothing.

- **Pull-request reviews and auto-merge:** review delete, submit and dismiss, review-comment resolve, and `CancelScheduledAutoMerge` check the reviewer, repo admin, or merge permission. Review lookups are scoped to the pull request and repo.

I found one real authorization gap, in the project-board API. I read the code only and didn't run any requests, so none of this has been exercised.

## Finding: project-board issue endpoints don't require write access to the issue

The routes in `routers/api/v1/api.go` only check that the caller can write to projects. The issue named in the `{issue_id}` path parameter is then loaded in `projectScope.findIssue` (`routers/api/v1/shared/project.go:114-146`), which checks at most read access.

Three handlers use it:
- **Add:** `AddIssueToProjectColumn` calls `findColumnIssue` at `routers/api/v1/shared/project.go:1834`, then `project_service.AddIssueToColumn` at `:1838`. That attaches the issue to the project through `IssueAssignOrRemoveProject`, which also writes a project comment on the issue timeline.
- **Remove:** `RemoveIssueFromProjectColumn` calls `findColumnIssue` at `:1957`, then `RemoveIssueFromColumn` at `:1961`.
- **Move:** `MoveProjectIssue` calls `scope.findIssue` at `:2103`, then `MoveIssueToColumn` at `:2108`.

**Owner-level boards** (`/orgs/{org}/projects/...`, `/user/projects/...`):
- `findIssue` looks the issue up by global ID and requires only `CanReadIssuesOrPulls` (`routers/api/v1/shared/project.go:138`).
- The route guards are `reqProjectsUnitAccess(Write)` for orgs (`routers/api/v1/api.go:1820`) and only `reqToken()` for `/user/projects` (`routers/api/v1/api.go:1172`).
- So an org member with org-wide project write can add, remove or move an issue in a repo where they only have read access. That includes private repos they can read.
- Cross-owner attachment is blocked by `CanBeAccessedByOwnerRepo` in `models/issues/issue_project.go:114`. The problem is within one owner.

**Repo-level boards** (`/repos/{owner}/{repo}/projects/...`):
- The route guard is `reqRepoWriter(unit.TypeProjects)` (`routers/api/v1/api.go:1754`).
- `findIssue` loads the issue with `GetIssueByRepoID` and does no permission check on it (`routers/api/v1/shared/project.go:119-121`).
- So a collaborator with projects-write but only issues-read can change issue-to-project membership.

**Web UI comparison:** the web UI requires both permissions. `routers/web/web.go:1389-1390` stacks `reqRepoIssuesOrPullsWriter` with `reqRepoProjectsReader` or `reqRepoProjectsWriter`. The API is weaker than the web UI.

**Fix:** after `findIssue` loads the issue, require `CanWriteIssuesOrPulls(issue.IsPull)` on the issue's repo, for both the repo-level and owner-level cases. Return 404 or 403 otherwise.

## Confirmed leaks

1. **`routers/private/internal.go:36`** is the most serious. `log.Debug("Forbidden attempt to access internal url: Authorization header: %s", tokens)` logs the whole `X-Gitea-Internal-Auth` header. That header is `Bearer <INTERNAL_TOKEN>`, and the line runs when authentication fails. A caller who is close to the right token, or who sends a valid token with some other fault, has the secret written to the debug log. The code comment at line 31 already notes that the token is passed in the clear.
2. **`modelmigration/v1_9/v85.go:71`** logs `token.Sha1`, the plaintext access token, together with the token name and user ID: `log.Warn("Unable to transform token %s with name %s ...", token.Sha1, ...)`. It runs only in the legacy migration, for tokens shorter than 8 characters. It still writes a live credential to the log.

## Likely leaks (depend on what the client sends)

3. **`services/packages/auth.go:64`** and **`services/actions/auth.go:83`** both do `log.Error("split token failed: %s", h)`, where `h` is the raw `Authorization` header. The branch runs when the header has no space, for example a bare token sent without a `Bearer ` prefix. That token is then logged at error level. The error returned to the client is generic (`"split token failed"`), so the HTTP response is fine.
3. **`services/auth/basic.go:61`** logs `uname` at trace level for password-based Basic auth. It is safe when the password is the token. But `services/auth/basic.go:140` logs `uname` for sign-in, and some clients put a token in the username field, so a token can end up in the trace log. This is low severity and only at trace level.

## Findings

1. **Codebase migration client has no allow/block-list check.** `services/migrations/codebase.go:88-97` builds a bare `http.Transport` with only `proxy.Proxy()`. Every other migration downloader uses `NewMigrationHTTPTransport()`, which applies the host allow/block lists (`services/migrations/http_client.go:39-41`). The base URL is hard-coded to `https://api3.codebasehq.com` (`codebase.go:81`), so a user can't point the first request at an internal host. The gap shows up if that host or an API response redirects to an internal address, because the client follows redirects with no dial-time check. Severity is low to medium.

2. **LFS client falls back to an unguarded transport.** `modules/lfs/http_client.go:37-42` uses a plain `http.Transport{Proxy: proxy.Proxy()}` when the caller passes a nil transport. It then talks to the endpoint from `NewClientFromEndpoint(cloneurl, lfsurl, …)` (`modules/lfs/client.go:38-47`), and that endpoint can come from the user-supplied `LFSEndpoint`. The production callers all pass the guarded `NewMigrationHTTPTransport()`:
   - `services/mirror/mirror_push.go:147`
   - `services/mirror/mirror_pull.go:184`
   - `services/migrations/gitea_uploader.go:133`, which feeds `services/repository/migrate.go:161`

   The risk is that any new caller, or a test-style `nil` as in `tests/integration/mirror_pull_test.go:61`, silently gets an SSRF-capable client. This is a latent hazard rather than a current hole.

3. **Proxies bypass the allow/block check.** `modules/hostmatcher/http.go:72-79` says that when a proxy is configured, the proxy dials the target, so Gitea's dial-time check only covers the proxy itself. This affects the webhook, migration, OpenID and OAuth-avatar clients (`services/webhook/deliver.go:317`, `services/migrations/http_client.go:40`, `modules/auth/openid/openid.go:37`, `routers/web/auth/oauth.go:316`). With `[proxy]` enabled, internal targets are only blocked if the proxy blocks them. The webhook proxy function does re-check the allow-list, but only by hostname (`services/webhook/deliver.go:295`). A hostname that resolves to an internal IP gets through that check.

4. **`uri.Open` defaults to an unguarded client.** `modules/uri/uri.go:25-27` calls `OpenWithClient(uriStr, http.DefaultClient)`. The migration code uses the guarded `OpenWithClient(..., getMigrationHTTPClient())` (`services/migrations/gitea_uploader.go:346`, `:594`), so there is no live issue now. It is a trap if someone calls plain `Open` with a user URL. `OpenWithClient` also accepts `file:` URLs (`uri.go:48`), which is a local file read if the caller doesn't restrict schemes.

5. **`httplib.NewRequest` uses an unguarded default transport.** `modules/httplib/request.go:148-153` falls back to `defaultTransport()` (`request.go:20`), which only sets `ProxyFromEnvironment` and a dial timeout. Its callers, `modules/private/internal.go:102` and `modules/public/vitedev.go:127`, use admin-configured URLs, so this is not exploitable today.

6. **Admin-configured endpoints, not user-controlled.** These use plain `http.DefaultClient` or a bare transport:
   - `modules/updatechecker/update_checker.go:31-37`
   - `modules/mcaptcha/mcaptcha.go:44-49`

   - `modules/hcaptcha/hcaptcha.go:58`

The code base already has an SSRF guard, so most paths are covered. I found one real gap and a few weaker ones. I read the code but didn't run any exploit.

**How the existing guard works.** `modules/hostmatcher/http.go:18-66` checks the resolved peer IP at dial time, against `ALLOWED_HOST_LIST` (default `external`) or the migration allow/block lists. It also covers redirects, because the check runs on every dial. These paths use it:
- Webhooks: `services/webhook/deliver.go:315-318`.
- Migration downloaders and asset downloads: `services/migrations/http_client.go:38-41`.
- OpenID: `modules/auth/openid/openid.go:35-37`.
- Gogs and OneDev downloaders (`services/migrations/gogs.go:106-115`, `onedev.go:88-95`) and the Gitea and GitLab asset clients (`gitea_downloader.go:276`, `gitlab.go:317`), through the migration transport.
- LFS fetches from pull mirrors, push mirrors and migrations (`services/mirror/mirror_pull.go:184`, `services/mirror/mirror_push.go:147`, `services/repository/migrate.go:161`), through the migration transport.

**Findings**

1. **Proxy path skips the check (webhooks, medium).**
   - `services/webhook/deliver.go:280-306` (`webhookProxy`) returns the proxy for hosts matching `PROXY_HOSTS`. In that case `NewDialContext` only sees the proxy address, so the target is never checked.
   - The `allowList.MatchHostName` check at `deliver.go:297` only matches IP literals and glob patterns. A hostname that resolves to `127.0.0.1` or `169.254.169.254` gets through.
   - The comment at `deliver.go:313-314` accepts this and leaves restricting targets to the proxy. If the proxy can reach internal addresses, a webhook URL can too.
   - The migration transport comments claim to cover the proxy path, but `NewHTTPTransport` doesn't do that either (`modules/hostmatcher/http.go:69-79`).

2. **Clone-URL check is resolve-then-use (import and mirrors, medium).**
   - `IsMigrateURLAllowed` (`services/migrations/migrate.go:44-84`) does its own `net.LookupIP` and ignores lookup errors, so the DNS answer can change before git connects.
   - The check is also done at request time only. The mirror and import actions that call it don't recheck at sync time, so a later DNS change isn't caught.
   - The `git clone` or `git fetch` subprocess itself connects without the dial-time guard, and git can follow redirects. A public URL that redirects to an internal host, or DNS rebinding, can reach internal git services.
   - Callers: `routers/web/repo/migrate.go:184`, `routers/api/v1/repo/migrate.go:103`, `routers/web/repo/setting/setting.go:327` and `:507`, `routers/api/v1/repo/mirror.go:359`, `routers/api/v1/repo/repo.go:1101`.

3. **Unguarded HTTP clients that make real requests.**
   - `modules/uri/uri.go:25-27` (`Open`) uses `http.DefaultClient`, which has no restriction. The migration code uses `OpenWithClient` with the guarded client, but any other caller of `Open` is exposed. I didn't find one in the non-test code, so this is a trap for future callers.
   - `modules/lfs/http_client.go:37-44` (`newHTTPClient`) falls back to a bare `http.Transport{Proxy: proxy.Proxy()}` when no transport is passed. `NewClientFromEndpoint` with a nil transport is therefore unguarded. The three callers listed above pass the guarded one.
   - `services/migrations/codebase.go:88-100` builds a client with no `hostmatcher`, only a proxy. The API base URL is fixed to `api3.codebasehq.com`, but any response link it follows would be unguarded. This is low risk.

4. **Operator-configured URLs (low).**
   - `modules/updatechecker/update_checker.go:31-35` and the captcha clients use `http.DefaultClient` or a plain transport. The captcha clients are `modules/recaptcha/recaptcha.go:41` and `modules/mcaptcha/mcaptcha.go:49`.
   - These targets come from admin config, not from users, so they are not user-controlled SSRF.

**Checked and not a server-side fetch.** `modules/avatar/federated.go:17-47` only does an SRV lookup to build a Libravatar URL, which the user's browser then loads. The server doesn't fetch the avatar.

**Not checked.** I didn't look at the OAuth2 login-source code beyond a grep, which found nothing. I didn't check the `openid.go:31` default list or the OpenID discovery path beyond the transport setup.

## Confirmed gaps

**1. Codebase migration client has no SSRF guard.** `services/migrations/codebase.go:88-98`
- It builds a bare `http.Transport` with only a proxy function. Every other downloader uses `NewMigrationHTTPTransport()`, which applies the allow/block lists.
- The requests go through `d.client.Do(req)` at `services/migrations/codebase.go:143`.
- Request URLs come from `d.baseURL.Parse(endpoint)` at `services/migrations/codebase.go:124`. The base is hard-coded to `https://api3.codebasehq.com`, so this is not directly attacker-steerable today. Still, none of the client's requests are validated, including any redirect or absolute URL that gets into the response data.
- The fix is to use `NewMigrationHTTPTransport()`, as `onedev.go` does.

**2. Git clone and mirror targets are checked once, not at connection time.**
- `IsMigrateURLAllowed` (`services/migrations/migrate.go:44-107`) resolves the hostname with `net.LookupIP` and checks the result against the lists.
- The clone later runs `git.CloneExternalRepo(ctx, opts.CloneAddr, ...)` at `services/repository/migrate.go:89`. Git does its own DNS lookup and follows its own HTTP redirects, and neither goes through the dial-time check.
- DNS rebinding (the name resolves to a public IP at check time and an internal IP at clone time) or an HTTP redirect to an internal host could reach internal services.
- The error from `net.LookupIP` is deliberately ignored (`services/migrations/migrate.go:84`). If a hostname doesn't resolve for Gitea but resolves for git, such as a split-horizon name, the check falls through to the hostname-only comparison.
- `ipAllowed` requires every resolved IP to match the allow list. `allowList.MatchHostName(hostName)` alone is enough to pass the check (`services/migrations/migrate.go:100-101`). An allow-listed name can therefore resolve to any IP and pass, because the block list only applies if it also contains private ranges.

**3. Configured proxies bypass the host checks.**
- `hostmatcher.NewDialContext` always allows a dial to the proxy host and port (`modules/hostmatcher/http.go:37-42`). The target is then not checked, and `NewHTTPTransport` documents this as the proxy's responsibility (`modules/hostmatcher/http.go:69-74`).
- The comment on `NewMigrationHTTPTransport` says the target is validated "on both the direct-dial and proxy paths" (`services/migrations/http_client.go:36-38`). That contradicts the code above. When `[proxy]` is enabled, migrations, OAuth avatars, OpenID discovery and webhooks can all reach internal addresses through the proxy.
- In the webhook proxy function, hosts that don't match `PROXY_HOSTS` fall through to `http.ProxyFromEnvironment` with no allow-list check (`services/webhook/deliver.go:304`). For hosts that do match, the check is `MatchHostName` only, so it ignores resolved IPs (`services/webhook/deliver.go:298`). An allowed-looking name can resolve to an internal IP behind the proxy.

**4. The update checker uses a bare transport.** `modules/updatechecker/update_checker.go:31-36`
- It has no host validation, only `proxy.Proxy()`. The endpoint comes from the admin setting `[cron.update_checker] ENDPOINT` (`httpEndpoint`), so this is admin-controlled, not user-controlled. I'm listing it for completeness.

## Main finding

**Codebase migration downloader skips the SSRF-checked transport.** `services/migrations/codebase.go:88-96` builds its client with a bare `http.Transport{Proxy: ...}`. It doesn't use `NewMigrationHTTPTransport()`, so none of the migration allow/block-list dial checks apply.

- The XML response is returned to the user.
- The pre-check `IsMigrateURLAllowed` (`services/migrations/migrate.go:44-77`) resolves the host once. A DNS-rebinding hostname can pass that check, and an HTTP redirect to `127.0.0.1`, `169.254.169.254` or `10.x` is not checked at all.

## Weaker findings

1. **Check-then-use for git clone and mirror.** `IsMigrateURLAllowed` (`services/migrations/migrate.go:70-77`) does a one-off `net.LookupIP` and ignores the lookup error: "it's safe to ignore the LookupIP error".
   - The actual `git clone`, `git fetch` and `git push` calls run in the git subprocess, which does its own DNS lookup and follows its own redirects.
   - So a rebinding hostname or a redirect can reach an internal address.
   - The hostname is only checked against the block list and allow list, so a hostname that resolves to nothing at check time can pass.

2. **`uri.Open` defaults to `http.DefaultClient`.** `modules/uri/uri.go:25-27` uses it with no host validation. It also accepts `file://` (`modules/uri/uri.go:44-45`).
   - I found no non-test callers of `uri.Open`. The two real uses (`services/migrations/gitea_uploader.go:346` and `:594`) pass `getMigrationHTTPClient()`.

I found three real gaps, plus one design caveat in the shared transport. Most of the URL-fetching paths are already guarded. This was a static read of the code; I didn't run any exploit.

## Findings

1. **Proxy path skips the target check, in all SSRF-guarded clients** — `modules/hostmatcher/http.go:37-42` and `modules/hostmatcher/http.go:69-81`
   - The allow/block check runs only inside the dialer. When a proxy is used, the dialer connects to the proxy host and the check always passes it (`http.go:38-41`). The final target is never checked.
   - The doc comment at `http.go:70-74` states that restricting proxied targets is the proxy's job.
   - Several callers inherit this:
     - Webhooks: the transport is built at `services/webhook/deliver.go:315-318`. `webhookProxy` (`deliver.go:280-306`) returns `http.ProxyFromEnvironment` for non-matching hosts and the fixed proxy for matching ones. For `ProxyHosts` matches it does call `allowList.MatchHostName(req.URL.Host)` (`deliver.go:298`), which is a hostname check only. A hostname that resolves to an internal IP passes it.
     - OpenID discovery: `modules/auth/openid/openid.go:35-38`.
     - OAuth2 avatar fetch: `routers/web/auth/oauth.go:312-317`.
   - This matters only if a proxy is configured. If one is, a user-supplied URL to `http://169.254.169.254/` or `http://10.x.x.x/` is requested through that proxy without a Gitea-side check.
   - The migration transport is the exception: its comment at `services/migrations/http_client.go:36-38` says it validates on both paths. But `http.go:75-81` doesn't do that, so I couldn't confirm the claim from the code I read.

2. **Codebase migration client has no SSRF transport** — `services/migrations/codebase.go:88-97`
   - It builds a bare `http.Transport` with only `Proxy` set. It doesn't use `NewMigrationHTTPTransport` like the other downloaders (`onedev.go:84`, `gogs.go:106`, `github.go:100`).
   - The API base URL is hardcoded to `https://api3.codebasehq.com` (`codebase.go:81`). That limits direct exposure, but any redirect or response-derived URL is followed with no dial-time check. The inconsistency should be fixed.

3. **LFS client falls back to an unguarded transport** — `modules/lfs/http_client.go:37-42`
   - When `httpTransport == nil`, it builds `&http.Transport{Proxy: proxy.Proxy()}` with no host check.
   - `NewClientFromEndpoint` (`modules/lfs/client.go:38-47`) passes the transport through unchanged. The callers I saw all pass a migration transport (`services/mirror/mirror_push.go:147`, `services/mirror/mirror_pull.go:184`). I didn't open `services/repository/migrate.go:161` (`httpTransport` is its own variable) or check whether any of these callers can pass `nil`.
   - The safe behavior depends on every caller remembering to pass the guarded transport. The user-controlled LFS endpoint, from `opts.LFSEndpoint` or the clone URL, is the SSRF vector if it's ever `nil`.

4. **Push mirror address isn't checked against the migration allow/block list** — `routers/api/v1/repo/mirror.go:357-389` and `routers/web/repo/setting/setting.go:505-537`
   - Both only run `git.ParseRemoteAddr`, which validates the URL's syntax, then `AddPushMirrorRemote`. Neither calls `IsMigrateURLAllowed` (`services/migrations/migrate.go:44`).
   - Pull mirrors and migrations do call it (`services/mirror/mirror_pull.go:120`, `services/migrations/migrate.go:111`).
   - On sync, git pushes to the stored remote address, so a user who can create push mirrors can point it at `http://localhost:...` or `http://10.x.x.x/...`. The LFS push at `mirror_push.go:147` does use the guarded transport. The `git push` itself isn't protected by Gitea's Go dialer, so I haven't confirmed that the git subprocess is blocked.

- Webhook delivery: `services/webhook/deliver.go:315`, direct dial path.
- Migration clients: `services/migrations/http_client.go:24-42`, `github.go:100`, `gitlab.go:97`, `gitea_downloader.go:87`, `gogs.go:106`, `onedev.go:84`.

I didn't find any `http.Get` or `DefaultClient` use in non-test, non-build code that handles user-supplied URLs.

Most outbound paths in this checkout are guarded. I found one clear SSRF gap and a few weaker ones. I only read the code; I didn't run anything.

**Guarded paths (no finding)**
- Webhook delivery uses `hostmatcher.NewHTTPTransport` at `services/webhook/deliver.go:311-317`, restricted by `ALLOWED_HOST_LIST`.
- The OAuth2 avatar fetch is guarded at `routers/web/auth/oauth.go:306-316`.
- OpenID discovery is guarded at `modules/auth/openid/openid.go:34-37`.
- The GitHub, GitLab, Gogs and OneDev migration clients use `NewMigrationHTTPTransport` (`services/migrations/http_client.go:36-42`).
- LFS during migration and mirror sync receives the guarded transport from its callers (`services/mirror/mirror_pull.go:184`, `services/mirror/mirror_push.go:147`).

**Findings**

1. **High: Codebase migration has no host check on the request.**
   - `services/migrations/codebase.go:88-96` builds a bare `http.Transport` whose only hook is `Proxy`, which sets basic auth and returns `proxy.Proxy()`. It doesn't use `NewMigrationHTTPTransport`, so the allow/block lists aren't applied at dial time.
   - `callAPI` (`services/migrations/codebase.go:~115`) then requests `baseURL` plus an endpoint.
   - The only protection is the one-time pre-check in `services/migrations/migrate.go:50-86`. That check has the weaknesses in finding 4, and a Codebase `CloneAddr` can reach internal addresses and redirect targets that it doesn't cover.
   - Any redirect from the first host to `169.254.169.254` or `127.0.0.1` is followed with no check, and the response is parsed into the migrated repository's data.
   - The fix is to use `NewMigrationHTTPTransport()` here, as the other downloaders do.

2. **Medium: the LFS client falls back to an unguarded transport.**
   - `modules/lfs/http_client.go:38-42` uses a plain `&http.Transport{Proxy: proxy.Proxy()}` when `httpTransport == nil`.
   - `NewClientFromEndpoint` (`modules/lfs/client.go:32-38`) passes the transport straight through.
   - The migration and mirror callers I found pass a guarded transport (`services/repository/migrate.go:161` passes `httpTransport`, which I didn't trace to its definition). The default is still unsafe for any caller that passes `nil`.
   - It also matters because `opts.LFSEndpoint` is user-supplied.
   - The fix is to make the default fail closed.

3. **Low: the captcha, update-check and URI fetchers use unguarded clients.**
   - These are `modules/turnstile/turnstile.go:22-26`, `modules/hcaptcha/hcaptcha.go:58`, `modules/recaptcha/recaptcha.go:41` and `modules/mcaptcha/mcaptcha.go:49`.
   - They use `http.DefaultClient` or a proxy-only transport.
   - Their URLs are admin-configured (or constants), so this is not user-reachable SSRF. It is only a hardening gap.
   - `modules/uri/uri.go:26` calls `OpenWithClient(uriStr, http.DefaultClient)`. I did not trace its callers, so I can't say whether user input reaches it. Check that before dismissing it.

4. **Low: the migration pre-check can be bypassed.**
   - In `services/migrations/migrate.go:~84-86`, `net.LookupIP` errors are deliberately ignored. A failed lookup leaves `addrList` empty, which then goes to `checkByAllowBlockList` (not read; whether that allows or rejects an empty list is unverified).
   - The check is also a one-time DNS resolution, so a DNS-rebinding hostname could resolve to a public address at check time and an internal one at connect time.
   - This only matters for downloaders that lack the dial-time guard, which today means finding 1. The git clone itself runs as a separate process and can't be guarded by the HTTP transport.

I found one clear SSRF gap. I also found two weaker spots (a time-of-check gap and a proxy bypass) and one item that isn't user-controlled. I read the code only and didn't run anything.

## Unprotected
**`services/migrations/codebase.go:88-97`** is the main finding. The Codebase migration downloader builds its own `http.Transport` with only a `Proxy` function and no dial-time host check. The target comes from the user-supplied clone address, parsed at `services/migrations/codebase.go:35-51`. Every API call goes through this client (`services/migrations/codebase.go:137`).

The other downloaders use `NewMigrationHTTPTransport()`, which checks each connection against the allow/block lists:
- GitHub: `services/migrations/github.go:98-118`
- OneDev: `services/migrations/onedev.go:84`
- Gogs: `services/migrations/gogs.go:108`

Codebase is the only one that skips it. The only protection is the one-time pre-check `IsMigrateURLAllowed` (`services/migrations/migrate.go:44`). That pre-check resolves DNS once and ignores lookup errors (`services/migrations/migrate.go:90-91`). A hostname that resolves differently at connect time (DNS rebinding), or an HTTP redirect to `127.0.0.1` or `169.254.169.254`, would get past it. The fix is to use `NewMigrationHTTPTransport()` here, with a wrapper for the basic-auth header as OneDev does.

## Weaker spots
- **`services/webhook/deliver.go:304`**: when `Webhook.ProxyURL` is set, a webhook URL that matches none of the `ProxyHosts` patterns falls back to `http.ProxyFromEnvironment`. That path never checks the allow-list. The code comment at `services/webhook/deliver.go:313-314` says this is deliberate: the proxy is responsible for blocking. It's only exploitable if the environment proxy can reach internal addresses.
- **`services/migrations/migrate.go:44-92`**: besides the Codebase gap above, every route that calls `IsMigrateURLAllowed` is only checked at request time. This matters for any code path that doesn't use the protected transport. The callers are:

## Findings

**1. Webhooks: no target check when a proxy is configured** (`services/webhook/deliver.go:251`, `services/webhook/deliver.go:315-318`, `modules/hostmatcher/http.go:75-81`)
- Webhook URLs (`w.URL`) are user-supplied. They're built into requests at `services/webhook/deliver.go:42,53,70,82`, `services/webhook/matrix.go:54` and `services/webhook/payloader.go:112`.
- The only check is the dialer `Control` hook. That hook sees the address Gitea dials, and with a proxy that is the proxy, not the webhook target.
- The code says so itself (`services/webhook/deliver.go:313`, `modules/hostmatcher/http.go:69-74`): checking the proxied target is "the proxy server's responsibility".
- `webhookProxy` (`services/webhook/deliver.go:279-300`) can route a request through the proxy, either when the host matches `ProxyHosts` or via `http.ProxyFromEnvironment`. The `allowList.MatchHostName` check at line 297 runs only for hosts that match `ProxyHosts`, and only by hostname. It never checks resolved IPs.
- Bypass: when a proxy is in use, a hostname like `localhost` or `169.254.169.254`, or a name that resolves to an internal IP, is not checked by Gitea, so a user who can create webhooks may reach internal services through the proxy. This only applies when the proxy can reach internal addresses.

**2. Every client built on `hostmatcher.NewHTTPTransport` has the same proxy hole** (`modules/hostmatcher/http.go:47-52`, `modules/hostmatcher/http.go:75-81`)
- Inside `NewDialContext`, `Control` returns `nil` whenever the dialed host and port equal the proxy, so the target is never validated on the proxy path.
- This affects:
  - OAuth2 avatar fetch: `routers/web/auth/oauth.go:314-318`, with the URL used at `routers/web/auth/oauth.go:324`. The URL comes from the OAuth provider's profile, which the provider controls.
  - OpenID verification and discovery: `modules/auth/openid/openid.go:35-37`. The OpenID identifier is user-supplied.
  - Migrations: `services/migrations/http_client.go:36-38`. The comment at `services/migrations/http_client.go:34-35` claims the proxy path is validated, but the code doesn't do that, so the comment is wrong.

**3. Migration/mirror URL check can be bypassed by DNS rebinding** (`services/migrations/migrate.go:44-82`)
- `IsMigrateURLAllowed` resolves the host once, at `services/migrations/migrate.go:77`, and checks the result. It ignores the `LookupIP` error.
- Callers:
  - `routers/web/repo/migrate.go:184,201`
  - `routers/api/v1/repo/migrate.go:103,130`
  - `routers/web/repo/setting/setting.go:327,357,507`
  - `routers/api/v1/repo/mirror.go:359`
  - `routers/api/v1/repo/repo.go:1101`
  - `services/mirror/mirror_pull.go:120`
- The actual `git clone` and `git fetch` run as a git subprocess. They resolve the name again and are not covered by the dialer-level check, so a rebinding hostname can pass the check and then resolve to an internal address. Git redirects are also not checked.

**4. Unguarded HTTP clients that only use `proxy.Proxy()`**
- `services/migrations/codebase.go:88-98`: the Codebase downloader uses a bare `http.Transport` with no allow or block list. The base URL and the URLs it follows are user-supplied for a migration.
- `modules/lfs/http_client.go:38-42`: when no transport is passed in, the LFS client falls back to a bare `http.Transport{Proxy: ...}`. Current callers pass the migration transport:
  - `services/mirror/mirror_pull.go:184`
  - `services/mirror/mirror_push.go:147`
  - `services/repository/migrate.go:161`
  - `services/migrations/gitea_uploader.go:135`
  Any future caller that passes `nil` would reach internal hosts. The LFS endpoint is user-controlled, and `NewClientFromEndpoint` is at `modules/lfs/client.go:38`.
- `modules/updatechecker/update_checker.go:31-35`: the endpoint comes from admin config, so it is low risk.
- `modules/auth/password/pwn/pwn.go:63` and `modules/hcaptcha/hcaptcha.go:58` use fixed or admin-configured endpoints. They aren't user-driven.

**5. OAuth2 and OpenID Connect auto-discovery** (`services/auth/source/oauth2/providers_openid.go:46`)
- `OpenIDConnectAutoDiscoveryURL` is passed to goth's `openidConnect.New`, which fetches it with Go's default HTTP client. I didn't read goth's code, so I can't confirm that.
- No allow or block list applies. Only admins can create auth sources, so this is lower severity, but it is an SSRF sink for a compromised or low-trust admin.

## Guarded paths
- The webhook direct-dial path is checked by default, because `ALLOWED_HOST_LIST` defaults to `external` (`modules/setting/security.go:27`).
- Migration downloaders use `NewMigrationHTTPTransport` with the migration allow and block lists:
  - GitHub (`services/migrations/github.go:98,115`)
  - Gogs (`services/migrations/gogs.go:105-117`)
  - OneDev (`services/migrations/onedev.go:84`)
- The GitLab, Gitea and GitHub asset downloads at `services/migrations/gitlab.go:337`, `services/migrations/gitea_downloader.go:302` and `services/migrations/github.go:378` use clients built from those downloaders.

## Suggested fix
Validate the target host or resolved IP before choosing a proxy. That can be a check in the proxy function, or a custom `RoundTripper` that resolves and checks the target, so the check doesn't depend on the dialed address. Also add the block and allow lists to the Codebase transport.

## Findings

**1. Proxied requests skip target validation (all `hostmatcher` clients).**
- `modules/hostmatcher/http.go:35-39` exempts the proxy's host and port inside the dialer's `Control` hook.
- The comment at `modules/hostmatcher/http.go:69-74` says restricting the proxied target is the proxy's job.
- When `[proxy]` is enabled, `proxy.Proxy()` (`modules/proxy/proxy.go:56-81`) sends traffic through the proxy. The dialer then only sees the proxy address, so the allow/block lists never check the real target.
- Any proxy that can reach internal hosts (localhost, 169.254.169.254, 10.x) therefore lets a user reach them.
- This affects:
  - webhooks: `services/webhook/deliver.go:315-318`
  - migrations: `services/migrations/http_client.go:39-41`
  - OpenID: `modules/auth/openid/openid.go:35-38`
  - OAuth2 avatar fetch: `routers/web/auth/oauth.go:312-317`

**2. Webhook proxy selector skips the allow-list for non-matching hosts.**
- In `webhookProxy` (`services/webhook/deliver.go:280-306`), a host that matches `ProxyHosts` is checked against the allow-list (`:295-298`).
- Every other host falls through to `http.ProxyFromEnvironment` at `:304` with no allow-list check.
- If `HTTP_PROXY` is set in the environment, those webhook requests reach internal targets through that proxy.

**3. Webhook delivery sends to the stored URL.**
- `services/webhook/deliver.go:42` and `:53` use `w.URL` directly. The matching sites are `services/webhook/matrix.go:54` and `services/webhook/payloader.go:112`.
- Direct connections are only checked at dial time by finding 1's `hostmatcher` client at `:251`. If the allow-list is relaxed (e.g. `ALLOWED_HOST_LIST=*` or `private`), nothing else stops internal targets.

**4. Migration pre-check can be bypassed with DNS rebinding.**
- `services/migrations/migrate.go:82-87` resolves the hostname once with `net.LookupIP` and ignores lookup errors.
- The actual `git clone` of `CloneAddr` is done by the git binary, which never goes through the `hostmatcher` dialer. A hostname can resolve to a public IP at check time and to an internal one at clone time.
- Because the lookup error is ignored, a name that fails to resolve at check time passes the check.
- `MigrateRepository` (`services/migrations/migrate.go:113-123`) applies the same pre-check to `LFSEndpoint`.

**5. LFS client with no validated transport by default.**
- `modules/lfs/http_client.go:37-42` builds a plain `http.Transport` with only `proxy.Proxy()` when the caller passes `nil`. No `hostmatcher` is involved.
- The migration, push-mirror and pull-mirror callers pass a validated transport:
  - `services/repository/migrate.go:161`
  - `services/mirror/mirror_pull.go:184`
  - `services/mirror/mirror_push.go:147`
- Any other or future caller of `NewClientFromEndpoint` (`modules/lfs/client.go:38`) that passes `nil` gets an unprotected client.
- `lfs.createRequest` (`modules/lfs/http_client.go:234-245`) sends requests to server-provided action hrefs.

**6. Unvalidated default clients (lower risk, mostly admin-configured URLs).**
- `modules/uri/uri.go:26`: `uri.Open` uses `http.DefaultClient`, with redirects and no validation. The migration callers use `OpenWithClient` (`services/migrations/gitea_uploader.go:346` and `:594`), but `Open` itself is unprotected.
- `modules/httplib/request.go:20-25` and `:148-152`: the default transport has no host checks. Its users are `modules/public/vitedev.go:127` and `modules/private/internal.go:102`, both internal-only.
- `modules/updatechecker/update_checker.go:30-35`: proxy only, no checks.
- Captcha and breach-check clients use `http.DefaultClient` against configured endpoints:
  - `modules/recaptcha/recaptcha.go:41`
  - `modules/mcaptcha/mcaptcha.go:49`
  - `modules/hcaptcha/hcaptcha.go:58`
  - `modules/auth/password/pwn/pwn.go:35`
  - `modules/turnstile/turnstile.go:23-25`

## Fix direction
- Validate the target host and resolved IPs before handing the request to a proxy. Alternatively, refuse the proxy for requests whose target fails the allow/block lists.
- Apply the allow-list in `webhookProxy`'s fallback path.
- Run the git clone through a pinned, resolved IP, or re-check after resolution.
- Make the LFS client require a validated transport instead of defaulting to `nil`.

I found three places that skip the host allow/block check. The rest of the outbound-request paths are covered. I only read the code and ran no requests, so none of this is confirmed by exploitation.

## Findings without the SSRF guard

1. **OpenID Connect auto-discovery URL**: `services/auth/source/oauth2/providers_openid.go:46`
   - `openidConnect.New(..., source.OpenIDConnectAutoDiscoveryURL, ...)` fetches the admin-supplied discovery URL with goth's default HTTP client.

2. **Codebase migration client**: `services/migrations/codebase.go:88-98`
   - It builds a plain `http.Transport` with only `Proxy: proxy.Proxy()`. It does not use `NewMigrationHTTPTransport()`, so it has no dial-time allow/block list.
   - The base URL is hardcoded to `api3.codebasehq.com` (`codebase.go:82`), so direct exposure is low. The gap is that redirects and URLs returned by that API aren't constrained.
   - Every other downloader uses the guarded transport: `github.go:98` and `:115`, `onedev.go:84`, `gogs.go:105`, `gitea_downloader.go:87` and `:276`.

3. **Default `uri.Open`**: `modules/uri/uri.go:26`
   - `Open` uses `http.DefaultClient` with no host check.
   - The migration callers use the guarded `OpenWithClient(..., getMigrationHTTPClient())` (`services/migrations/gitea_uploader.go:346` and `:594`). I found no other callers of `Open`.
   - Anyone who calls it later with a user-supplied URI gets an unguarded fetch.

## Recommendation

Give the OIDC provider a guarded client, either by injecting an `http.Client` built with `hostmatcher.NewHTTPTransport` or by setting goth's HTTP client. Switch Codebase to `NewMigrationHTTPTransport()`. Make `uri.Open` refuse remote URLs, or require a client.

   - It's called from `routers/web/repo/migrate.go:184,201`, `routers/api/v1/repo/migrate.go:103,130`, `routers/web/repo/setting/setting.go:327,357,507`, `routers/api/v1/repo/mirror.go:359`, `routers/api/v1/repo/repo.go:1101` and `services/mirror/mirror_pull.go:120`.
   - The git subprocess does the connecting and doesn't go through the guarded transport. Redirects that git follows after the check also aren't covered.
   - The `file:` scheme is gated separately by `CanImportLocal`.

3. **Webhook requests that go through a proxy aren't checked.** `services/webhook/deliver.go:311-313` says outright that when `webhookProxy` routes a request through a configured proxy, restricting the target is the proxy's job. For hosts matching `ProxyHosts` (`deliver.go:296-301`), the allow-list is checked only on the host name. Other proxied requests are not checked at all. So a webhook URL pointing at an internal host can reach it if the proxy can. This is a configuration risk rather than a code bug.

4. **Latent: `uri.Open` uses `http.DefaultClient`.** `modules/uri/uri.go:25-27` accepts any http/https URL with no validation, and it follows redirects. I found no non-test callers, but a future caller would have no protection. Also `uri.Open`'s `file:` branch (`uri.go:42-43`) reads local files.

5. **Outbound calls to admin-configured URLs aren't validated.** These are not user-controllable, so they only matter if an admin can be tricked into setting a bad URL:
   - Update checker: `modules/updatechecker/update_checker.go:30-38`.
   - Captcha providers: `modules/hcaptcha/hcaptcha.go:58`, `modules/recaptcha/recaptcha.go:41` and `modules/mcaptcha/mcaptcha.go:49`.
   - The pwned-passwords client: `modules/auth/password/pwn/pwn.go:35`.
   - Minio: `modules/storage/minio.go:191-193`.
   - Elasticsearch: `modules/indexer/internal/elasticsearch/indexer.go:68-70`.

I found no clear, exploitable IDOR in the ID-taking handlers under `routers/`. Almost every handler that takes an ID from a URL parameter or form value either scopes the lookup to the owner or repo, or checks ownership right after loading the record. I swept `routers/web` and `routers/api/v1` for ID lookups driven by URL or form parameters, and read the candidate handlers. `services/`, `modules/` and the `routers/api/` packages other than `v1` weren't swept. Some `routers/api/v1` packages, such as `v1/org`, `v1/admin` and `v1/packages`, only got a parameter grep and weren't read.

## Weak spots (not exploitable)

- **`web/repo/setting/collaboration.go:207`**: `DeleteTeam` loads a team with `GetTeamByID(ctx, ctx.FormInt64("id"))`. It doesn't check that the team belongs to the repo's owner org, so the lookup is unscoped. The only action is `RemoveRepositoryFromTeam` for this repo, after the `canManageRepoCollaboratorTeam` check. A foreign team can be named, but the call only removes this repo from it, which does nothing if the team doesn't have it. This is a missing-scope smell, not a breach.
- **`web/repo/setting/collaboration.go:123` and `:139`**: `ChangeCollaborationAccessMode` and `DeleteCollaboration` take a user ID from the form with `GetUserByID`. That is only a target-user lookup. The repo-admin route middleware gates the action, and the operation is scoped to `ctx.Repo.Repository`.
- **`web/org/projects.go:320`**: `milestoneID` comes from `ctx.FormInt64("milestone")` and goes into `IssuesOptions.MilestoneIDs` without a check that the milestone belongs to the project's repos. It is only a filter, and the issue search is scoped to `Owner` and its repos. At worst it returns nothing.
- **`web/repo/issue_content_history.go:133`**: the comment is loaded from `history.CommentID`, with no `RepoID` check on the comment itself. `GetIssueContentHistoryAndPrev` at `:186` is called with `issue.ID`, which ties the history to the issue. Safe in practice.

I found no clear IDOR in the handlers I traced. Almost every handler that takes an ID from a URL parameter or form re-checks it against the repo, owner or doer before using it. ## Weak spots

1. **`routers/web/repo/setting/collaboration.go:207`** (`DeleteTeam`)

2. **`routers/api/v1/repo/issue_comment_attachment.go:361`** (`getIssueCommentSafe`)
   - When `CanReadIssuesOrPulls` fails, the function returns `nil` without writing any response. The caller then returns an empty 200.

I found no web or API endpoint that lacks any cross-origin protection and does something dangerous. Gitea no longer uses a `_csrf` token (`services/context/context.go:173-174`), so the check is different from the one you described. The remaining gaps are all low impact.

**How protection works now.** Gitea calls Go's `http.CrossOriginProtection.Check`, which rejects cross-origin state-changing requests using `Sec-Fetch-Site`/`Origin`. The call is made inside `verifyAuthWithOptions` (`routers/web/web.go:224-229`). A web route is protected only if it passes through one of these middlewares: `reqSignIn`, `optSignIn`, `optExploreSignIn`, `adminReq` or `crossOriginProtect`. Every state-changing route I read in `registerWebRoutes` (`web.go`, lines 342-1790) carries one of them except the ones below.

**Web routes**

1. `routers/web/web.go:549` – `POST /-/web-banner/dismiss` has no middleware. It only sets a dismissal cookie, so impact is negligible. Compare line 551, where `/-/web-theme/apply` explicitly adds `crossOriginProtect`.
2. `routers/web/web.go:757-773` – the `/user` group has no middleware, so none of these get the check:
   - `POST /user/activate` (759)
   - `Any /user/activate_email` (760). It accepts any method and activates an email from `code`/`email` query parameters (`routers/web/auth/auth.go:903-928`). It is token-gated and idempotent, so impact is low.
   - `POST /user/recover_account` (763)
   - `POST /user/forgot_password` (765)
   - `GET /user/logout` (766). Logout is a state change over GET, so any site can force a logout. Sign-out also writes to `ctx.Session` in `routers/web/auth/auth.go:451-470`.
3. `routers/web/web.go:582-617` – the `/user` group with `reqSignOut` covers these POSTs:
   - `POST /user/login` (583)
   - `POST /user/sign_up` (600)
   - `POST /user/link_account_signin` (602)
   - `POST /user/link_account_signup` (603)
   - `POST /user/two_factor` (606)
   - `POST /user/two_factor/scratch` (608)
   - `POST /user/webauthn/passkey/login` (613)
   - `POST /user/webauthn/assertion` (615)

   `reqSignOut` deliberately skips the check (`web.go:224`, `!options.SignOutRequired`), so these have no cross-origin protection. Login CSRF is the realistic risk here.
4. `routers/web/web.go:630-633` – `/login/oauth/userinfo`, `/access_token` and `/introspect` use `optSignInFromAnyOrigin`, which turns the check off (`web.go:336`). The comment at `web.go:331-335` says this is deliberate: CORS handles those routes, and git/LFS clients send no `Sec-Fetch-Site`. The same applies to the git and LFS routes at `web.go:1757` and `web.go:1762`.

**API routes (`routers/api/v1/api.go`)**

The API auth group has no cookie-session method. It uses only `OAuth2`, `HTTPSign`, `Basic` and optionally `ReverseProxy` (`api.go:902-911`). A cross-site request therefore can't carry ambient session credentials, and `reqToken` (`api.go:366-373`) requires a real signed-in user. The API's state-changing endpoints don't need a CSRF check, and I found no gap there.

The one caveat is `ReverseProxy` auth (`api.go:909`, enabled by `EnableReverseProxyAuthAPI`). It trusts a proxy-supplied header, which a browser would send automatically, so it's worth a look if you enable it.

It only runs inside the `verifyAuthWithOptions` middleware (`routers/web/web.go:181-229`), so a web route is protected only if one of those middlewares is attached to it. I found no CSRF gap. `routers/api/v1/api.go:902-913` builds the auth group from OAuth2/Bearer token, HTTPSign and Basic auth only (plus optional reverse proxy).
